dedupe_keys.name: iig empirical model of the equatorial electrojet indian sector

description: The Indian Institute of Geomagnetism has developed an empirical model of the equatorial electrojet, an intense current jet that flows in the upper atmosphere at about 105 to 110 kilometres, a few hundred kilometres wide (around 600 kilometres) and centred on the geomagnetic equator. The model predicts the diurnal, seasonal and solar activity variations in the intensity of this current over the Indian longitude sector, based on long-term observations from the Indian sector. The page explains that the electrojet gives insight into equatorial ionospheric electrodynamics, which affect satellite orbits, GPS, satellite communication links and electrical power grids. Licence: not stated for the resource; the describing article (doi:10.1029/2024sw003988) is CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0. Caveats: the page does not offer code or an online calculator, and the model applies to the Indian sector only. Coverage is India and the equatorial region at Indian longitudes. It supports hazard exposure studies of space weather effects on GNSS and power grids near the magnetic equator; related records are the NICT space weather forecast and the INGV eSWua service.
